sections.heading: Flashing Repair or Roof Replacement: The 25% Rule in New Jersey

runs.v: Does a roofer do flashing? Yes. Flashing is roofing work, done as a stand-alone repair or during a roof replacement, when worn step flashing, drip edge, and pipe boots are replaced, not reused, under a new roof. How do I fix the flashing on my roof? A lifted lap can be re-secured, but corroded or wrongly installed metal must be replaced with new flashing lapped in shingle fashion, a job for a roofer.

What is the 25% rule for roofing? In New Jersey, under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, repairing more than 25% of the roof of a commercial, multi-family, or attached building within 12 months requires a permit, and many roofers treat damage past about 25% of the roof as the point where replacement beats more repairs. A residential roof replacement typically takes one to two days; tear-offs expose the deck for new flashing.
